title: Unbounded degree overhead for Alice-conditioned quantum Bell certificates
abstract: Requiring each sum-of-squares term to involve only one of Alice's measurement questions can impose an unbounded certification cost. In the simplest Bell scenario, we prove that no finite level of the Alice-conditioned NPA hierarchy contains all standard level-two Bell certificates. An explicit family of truncated positive functionals on the infinite dihedral group exceeds the tilted-CHSH quantum bound at every prescribed finite level, while a standard degree-two certificate is exact. A Fejer-weighted trace reduces positivity to a rank-one subtraction from a moving-average Gram matrix. The required conditioned level grows at least as $(2-α)^{-1/2}$ near the endpoint tilt. This bounds the degree of exact nice-SOS inputs to compiled-game soundness proofs. Consequently, no finite conditioned level certifies the entire optimal CHSH randomness tradeoff against quantum side information, although standard level two does. Away from the endpoint, we prove a sharp one-level cost throughout $α\in[13/10,3/2]$, using optimal-strategy kernels and exact Bernstein matrix positivity to certify a continuous interval. The results separate ordinary SOS degree from the resources keyed by single-question certificate structure.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the resource cost associated with certifying quantum Bell inequalities when the certification process is conditioned on a single measurement choice by Alice. It proves that this conditioning introduces an unbounded overhead in the required degree of the polynomial certificate compared to standard methods. The findings help separate the computational resources needed for different structural assumptions in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates the additional degree overhead required when certifying quantum Bell inequalities using certificates conditioned on a single measurement choice by Alice.
main_result: It proves that the required conditioned certification level grows unboundedly as the system approaches certain limits, separating the resource requirements of single-question conditioning from standard SOS degree bounds.
method: The authors use Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations formulated as Sum-of-Squares (SOS) polynomials, constructing explicit counterexamples using truncated positive functionals on the infinite dihedral group.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum Bell inequalities, specifically the CHSH inequality, analyzed through the Navascués–Pironio–Acín (NPA) hierarchy and its specialized Alice-conditioned variants.
key_observables: The primary observables are the SDP values ($\omega_{std}^k$ vs. $\omega_{os}^k$) for standard and Alice-conditioned Bell certificates, and the resulting quantum-bound curve $\alpha(u)$.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the conditioning parameter $\alpha$, the certificate level $k$, and the distance $\epsilon$ to the endpoint tilt.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing the required degree for exact certification against the standard degree, and distinguishing between exact closure and finite-tolerance numerical saturation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the unbounded cost, showing the required conditioned degree diverging from the standard degree as the distance to the endpoint decreases.
paper_structure: The paper develops results by first showing the unbounded overhead (Theorem 1), then establishing continuous exact certification over an interval (Theorem 2), and finally refuting conjectures about fixed-level containment (Theorem 8.2).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to quantify the computational complexity of verifying quantum nonlocality, which is fundamental to quantum information theory and device-independent security protocols.
